---
title: "Option Greeks — Review"
---

## Greeks — Overview

| Greek | Symbol | Definition | BS Formula (call) |
|---------|---------|-----------|-------------------|
| Delta | Δ | $\partial c / \partial S$ | $N(d_1)$ |
| Gamma | Γ | $\partial \Delta / \partial S = \partial^2 c / \partial S^2$ | $N'(d_1) / (S_0 \sigma \sqrt{T})$ |
| Theta | Θ | $\partial c / \partial t$ | $-\frac{S_0 N'(d_1)\sigma}{2\sqrt{T}} - rKe^{-rT}N(d_2)$ |
| Vega | ν | $\partial c / \partial \sigma$ | — |
| Rho | ρ | $\partial c / \partial r$ | — |

::: {.callout-note title="Put vs. Call"}
$\Delta_p = N(d_1) - 1$ | $\Theta_p = -\frac{S_0 N'(d_1)\sigma}{2\sqrt{T}} + rKe^{-rT}N(-d_2)$ | $\Gamma$ **identical** for call and put
:::

---

## Black-Scholes Reminder

$$c = S_0 N(d_1) - Ke^{-rT}N(d_2) \qquad p = Ke^{-rT}N(-d_2) - S_0 N(-d_1)$$

$$d_1 = \frac{\ln(S_0/K) + (r + \sigma^2/2)T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}} \qquad d_2 = d_1 - \sigma\sqrt{T}$$

$$N'(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-x^2/2}$$

---

## Hedging Strategies — Comparison

| Strategy | Principle | Main Risk |
|-----------|---------|-----------------|
| Naked (Naked) | Do nothing | Unlimited loss if $S_T \gg K$ |
| Covered (Covered) | Buy shares at $t=0$ | Capital tied up, loss if $S_T \ll S_0$ |
| Stop-loss | Buy if $S_t > K$, sell if $S_t < K$ | High transaction costs, oscillations around $K$ |
| **Delta hedge** | Hold $\Delta$ shares per option | Continuous rebalancing required |

::: {.callout-important title="Pitfall — Stop-loss"}
$\text{stop-loss cost} = \max(S_0 - K, 0) \neq c_{\text{BS}}$ because : (1) discounting of cash flows, (2) ambiguity at point $S_t = K$.
:::

---

## Delta (Δ)

**Value ranges :**

- Call : $\Delta_c \in [0, 1]$
- Put : $\Delta_p \in [-1, 0]$
- Relation : $\Delta_c - \Delta_p = 1$

**Behavior by moneyness :**

| Moneyness | $\Delta_c$ (approx.) |
|-----------|---------------------|
| OTM ($S \ll K$) | $\approx 0$ |
| ATM ($S \approx K$) | $\approx 0{,}5$ |
| ITM ($S \gg K$) | $\approx 1$ |

**Delta Hedge — shares to trade :**

| Position | Buy | Sell |
|----------|---------|--------|
| Short call | — | $\Delta_c \times N_{\text{options}}$ |
| Long call | $\Delta_c \times N_{\text{options}}$ | — |
| Short put | $|\Delta_p| \times N_{\text{options}}$ | — |
| Long put | — | $|\Delta_p| \times N_{\text{options}}$ |

::: {.callout-tip title="Quick example"}
Short 2 000 calls, $\Delta_c = 0{,}6$ → buy $1\,200$ shares.
If $S : 100 \to 101$ → $c : 10 \to 10{,}6$ → profit $= 1200 \times 1 - 2000 \times 0{,}6 = 0$ ✓
:::

---

## Theta (Θ)

**General rule :** $\Theta < 0$ (time decay)

**Exceptions** (Θ can be > 0) :

- European put without dividend (deep ITM option)
- Call with very high rate $r$

**Behavior by moneyness ($T \to 0$) :**

| Moneyness | $\Theta$ as $T \to 0$ |
|-----------|------------------------|
| OTM | $\to 0$ |
| ITM | Plateau (intrinsic value dominates) |
| ATM | **Diverges to $-\infty$** ⚠️ |

::: {.callout-important title="Θ cannot be hedged"}
Time is certain → no hedging possible. Θ is the **daily cost** of holding a long option.
:::

---

## Gamma (Γ)

**Key property :** $\Gamma > 0$ **always** (long position)

**Behavior :**

- **Maximum** when ATM
- **Explodes** when ATM and $T \to 0$ ⚠️
- $\to 0$ at maturity for ITM/OTM

**Taylor expansion (price approximation) :**

$$\boxed{\delta c \approx \Theta\,\delta t + \Delta\,\delta S + \tfrac{1}{2}\Gamma\,\delta S^2}$$

- $\Delta\,\delta S$ : linear term → hedged by Delta hedge
- $\frac{1}{2}\Gamma\,\delta S^2$ : quadratic term → **residual gap** after Delta hedge

---

## Portfolio and Greeks

**Additivity :**

$$\Delta_\Pi = \sum_i w_i \Delta_i \qquad \Theta_\Pi = \sum_i w_i \Theta_i \qquad \Gamma_\Pi = \sum_i w_i \Gamma_i$$

**Making a portfolio Gamma-neutral :**

1. Choose a hedging option with $\Gamma_T$
2. Add $w_T = -\Gamma_\Pi / \Gamma_T$ options → $\Gamma$ neutralized
3. Recalculate $\Delta_\Pi$ → Delta has changed
4. Trade the **underlying** to restore $\Delta$-neutrality

::: {.callout-tip title="Example"}
$\Gamma_\Pi = -3\,000$, hedging option : $\Delta_T = 0{,}62$, $\Gamma_T = 1{,}5$

→ Buy $3000/1{,}5 = 2\,000$ options → $\Delta_\Pi$ becomes $2000 \times 0{,}62 = 1\,240$

→ Sell $1\,240$ shares to restore $\Delta$-neutrality
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Golden rule"}
**Modify Γ** → trade **options** (the underlying has $\Gamma = 0$)

**Modify Δ** → trade the **underlying** or options
:::

---

## Θ–Γ Triangle

::: {.callout-warning title="Fundamental trade-off"}
**Long Gamma** portfolio (Γ > 0) → **very negative Θ** (high daily cost)

**Short Gamma** portfolio (Γ < 0) → **positive Θ** (collects time value) but risk on large moves
:::

---

## Practical Management

- **Delta** : **daily** rebalancing
- **Gamma, Theta, Vega** : calculated and monitored, action if thresholds exceeded

---

## Black-Scholes Limits & Extensions

| Limit | Alternative Model |
|--------|------------------|
| Constant volatility (smile ignored) | **Heston** (stochastic vol) |
| No jumps | **Merton** Jump-Diffusion |
| American options (early exercise) | **Binomial/trinomial trees** |
| Complex relationships | **Neural networks, LSTM** |
| Optimal dynamic hedging | **Reinforcement Learning** |

**Greek Computation Methods :**

| Method | Cost | Precision |
|---------|------|----------|
| Finite differences | $O(n)$ evaluations | Approximate |
| Monte Carlo (LRM, Adjoint) | Variable | Good |
| **Automatic Differentiation (AD)** | $O(1)$ (adjoint mode) | **Exact** |

## American Put — Comparison Example

Parameters : $S_0 = K = 100$, $r = 5\%$, $\sigma = 20\%$, $T = 1$ year, $q = 2\%$

| Method | Price | Delta |
|---------|------|-------|
| Black-Scholes (European) | 9,23 USD | 0,587 |
| Binomial tree (American) | 7,50 USD | 0,530 |
| Monte Carlo (American) | 7,55 USD | 0,520 |
